name: PostgreSQL
tagline: Share a local Postgres replica with remote agents without handing over the keys to prod.
intro: The archived PostgreSQL reference server exposes one query tool and wraps queries in a read-only transaction. MCPWire filters by tool name; it does not inspect SQL or turn a general SQL tool into a read-only one.

tools.name: query
tools.note: Runs SQL inside the reference server’s read-only transaction. Keep database credentials read-only as well.

requirements: Provide a working PostgreSQL connection URL. Use database credentials with read-only permissions. This is an archived reference server.

name: GitHub
tagline: Share repo research and issue triage — never push_files or fork_repository.
intro: The official GitHub MCP server mixes read tools with destructive ones that act on YOUR token: push_files, fork_repository, merge_pull_request. MCPWire's firewall lets a peer's agent search repos and read issues while every write path stays invisible.
requirements: Set GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the host environment. This is the archived reference server.

name: Git
tagline: Remote code review over P2P: git_log and git_diff in, git_commit and git_reset out.
intro: The official Git MCP server operates on a local working copy. Teleport the inspection tools and an outside agent can review your uncommitted work end-to-end — while add/commit/reset never leave your machine.
requirements: Install uv (which provides uvx). Point --repository at an existing Git checkout.

name: Brave Search
tagline: Lend your Brave API quota to a teammate's agent — key never leaves your machine.
intro: The official Brave Search MCP server needs a BRAVE_API_KEY the remote peer doesn't have. Teleport the capability instead: their LLM searches the web through your tunnel, your credential stays in your env, and the DLP shield scrubs any key that leaks into output.
requirements: Set BRAVE_API_KEY in the host environment. This is the archived reference server.

name: Fetch
tagline: Give an agent URL fetching from your network position — rate-limited by your kill-switch.
intro: The official Fetch server turns an LLM into a curl with markdown conversion. Shared raw it lets a peer's agent request anything your machine can reach (including localhost). Use --max-calls and --ttl to keep it on a short leash.

tools.name: fetch
tools.note: GETs any URL reachable from YOUR machine, including internal hosts.

requirements: Install uv (which provides uvx). Requests need network access.

name: Puppeteer
tagline: Drive a headless Chrome on your machine from a remote agent, safely sandboxed.
intro: The official Puppeteer server runs a real browser on the host. Teleport it when a teammate's agent needs to render or screenshot a page that only your machine can reach — puppeteer_evaluate is the tool to think twice about, since it executes arbitrary JS in page context.

tools.name: puppeteer_fill
tools.note: Fills inputs — could type into logged-in sessions.

requirements: Requires a supported browser installation. This is the archived reference server.

name: Playwright
tagline: Accessibility-tree browser automation, teleported with a call ceiling.
intro: Microsoft's Playwright MCP drives a browser via accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots. Sharing it over MCPWire gives a remote agent a real browser on your machine — pair --confirm with browser_click and browser_type so nothing happens without your y/n.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.note: Types into fields — could type credentials.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.note: Runs arbitrary JS in the page.

name: Memory (Knowledge Graph)
tagline: Share a knowledge graph read-only — or let trusted agents write to theirs.
intro: The official Memory server persists an entity/relation graph in a JSON file. Teleport the read tools to let any agent ground its answers in your graph, and gate the mutating tools behind --confirm.

name: Sequential Thinking
tagline: The zero-risk demo: one stateless reasoning tool, perfect first teleport.
intro: The reference sequential thinking server maintains a reasoning scratchpad for each server process. Share its single tool to try the connection without cloud credentials.

name: Slack
tagline: Remote agents read your Slack history; posting stays behind your y/n.
intro: The official Slack server authenticates with YOUR bot token. Teleport the listing/search tools so a teammate's agent can research threads, and put slack_post_message behind Human-in-the-Loop confirmation so nothing ships to a channel without you.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.note: Posts to channels as your bot.

requirements: Set SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_TEAM_ID in the host environment. This is the archived reference server.

name: Docker
tagline: Inspect containers and images from a remote machine; no run/stop teleported.
intro: This community Docker MCP server operates on the host Docker daemon. Expose container and image inspection tools while blocking container and image mutation.
requirements: Install uv (uvx) and run a Docker daemon accessible to the host. The server uses the Docker SDK environment configuration.

name: Kubernetes
tagline: Debug a cluster from a teammate's terminal — scale and delete stay with you.
intro: Kubernetes MCP servers act on your kubeconfig: listing pods is diagnostics, scaling a deployment is an incident. MCPWire's firewall splits the two cleanly, and --ttl makes the access window explicit.

tools.name: kubectl_get
tools.note: Reads Kubernetes resource state; use least-privilege kubeconfig credentials.

tools.name: kubectl_logs
tools.note: Reads application logs, which may contain secrets.

requirements: Install kubectl and configure a kubeconfig with access to your cluster. Helm is optional.

name: Stripe
tagline: Revenue research for remote agents — refunds and customer creation stay local.
intro: Stripe's agent toolkit speaks directly to your billing account with a secret key. Never paste that key into a teammate's config: teleport the read-only tools over MCPWire and the credential physically never leaves your machine.

tools.name: list_customers
tools.note: Customer records contain PII — keep DLP on.

requirements: Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in the host environment. Use a restricted API key with only the permissions you intend to share.

name: Sentry
tagline: Issue triage for on-call buddies — read-only by construction.
intro: Sentry's MCP server is designed around read-heavy issue triage, which makes it an ideal teleport target: a teammate helping you debug gets stack traces and tags through the tunnel, and the DLP shield scrubs tokens that appear in event payloads.

tools.name: search_issues
tools.note: Searches issues; AI-powered search may require a provider key.

tools.name: get_sentry_resource
tools.note: Reads Sentry resources that can include private data.

tools.name: execute_sentry_tool
tools.note: Generic operation dispatcher; do not expose it as a substitute for a narrow tool allowlist.

requirements: Set SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN on the host, or complete the server’s device-code login. AI-powered search may additionally require an LLM provider key.

name: Supabase
tagline: Project admin and SQL over P2P — expose introspection, keep DDL locked.
intro: Supabase's MCP server authenticates with a personal access token and can run arbitrary SQL plus management APIs. Teleport the introspection tools (tables, logs) and keep execute_sql behind --confirm or blocked entirely.
requirements: Set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN in the host environment and replace YOUR_PROJECT_REF with your project reference.

name: Context7 (Docs)
tagline: Up-to-date library docs for any agent — fully safe to teleport.
intro: Context7 resolves library documentation for LLMs. Every tool is read-only web access, so it's the classic 'capability share': your subscription/quota serves the peer, the key never moves, and zero destructive surface exists.

tools.name: resolve-library-id
tools.note: Maps a name to a Context7 library.

requirements: Network access is required. Configure a Context7 API key if your plan requires one.

name: Google Maps
tagline: Geocoding and directions powered by your API key, not theirs.
intro: The official Google Maps server needs a billable API key. Share the capability instead of the credential: a remote agent geocodes and plans routes through your tunnel with a --max-calls ceiling so the bill stays boring.
requirements: Set GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY in the host environment. This is the archived reference server.

name: Time
tagline: Timezone math for agents — the hello-world of safe teleports.
intro: The official Time server converts times across zones. It is completely stateless and read-only: a perfect smoke test that a peer's MCP client is wired to your tunnel correctly.
requirements: Install uv (which provides uvx). No credentials required.

name: Everything (Test Server)
tagline: The MCP reference server — teleport it to test every protocol feature.
intro: The Everything reference server exercises MCP tools, resources, prompts and notifications. Expose the basic demonstration tools while keeping environment inspection and file access tools outside the allowlist.

tools.name: gzip-file-as-resource
tools.note: Reads and compresses a local file.

name: Notion
tagline: Second-brain search for remote collaborators — edits need your approval.
intro: Notion's MCP server authenticates against your workspace with an integration token. Teleport search/fetch so a teammate's agent can ground answers in your docs, and keep create/update endpoints out of the tools/list entirely.

tools.name: API-post-search
tools.note: Searches pages shared with the integration.

tools.name: API-patch-page
tools.note: Updates page properties, including archive state.

requirements: Set NOTION_TOKEN in the host environment, and share the intended pages with that Notion integration.

name: Figma
tagline: Design-to-code context for outside agents — read-only by nature.
intro: The Figma Context MCP server extracts layout and styling data from your Figma files so coding agents can implement designs. It's read-only against the Figma API, making it a safe, high-value teleport: your API key, their agent, zero credentials exchanged.
requirements: Set FIGMA_KEY in the host environment before running the example.

name: MongoDB
tagline: Aggregate and inspect a remote cluster; inserts and deletes never leave home.
intro: MongoDB's MCP server connects with your connection string — the single most sensitive credential in a stack. Teleport find/aggregate and the peer's agent explores data through your tunnel; the connection string never crosses the wire.

tools.name: list-connections
tools.note: Lists connection IDs for use with the database tools.

tools.name: find
tools.note: Reads documents that may contain private data.

tools.name: aggregate
tools.note: Reads aggregation results; review access to private data.

requirements: Set MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING in the host environment. The example enables the server’s own read-only mode.

name: Netlify
tagline: Deploy logs and site status for collaborators — deploys stay behind the firewall.
intro: Netlify's MCP server manages sites with your account token. Teleport the read/observability tools so a collaborator's agent can debug builds, and gate deploy operations behind Human-in-the-Loop approval.

tools.name: netlify-observability-get-request-logs
tools.note: Reads request logs, which can contain private data.

requirements: Requires Node.js 22 or newer. Authenticate on the host, or set NETLIFY_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. The --verbose flag exposes individual operation tools so they can be filtered separately.

name: Redis
tagline: Cache introspection over P2P — GET allowed, DEL and FLUSHALL never.
intro: Redis MCP servers talk to your cache with full command power. The dangerous ones are exactly what they sound like: DEL and FLUSHALL against production. Whitelist reads and information commands, and let the firewall make everything else nonexistent to the peer.

tools.name: get
tools.note: Reads a value; may contain private data.

requirements: Install uv (uvx) and point --url at a running Redis instance. Configure Redis ACL credentials to restrict the accessible data and operations.
